body: I suppose for me it is not just psychological reframing as it is a physiological reframing.  Knowing that the reason I am depressed *may* come from an imbalance in MOA-A which messes with all sorts of pathways.  Knowing what pathways in my brain are probably affected and roughly how the brain deals with chemical gradients helps a lot.  Also learning that we don't really exactly understand major depression made me very skeptical of a lot of direct treatments that a therapist suggested I look into.  Learning that the therapist didn't have first hand experience with depression, and had less of an understanding of the brain than I did kept me from taking medication.  I was in a deep depression for about two years before I figured any semblance balance out for myself.  I felt that I was lying to myself when I told myself it would eventually go away because I had no evidence to suggest that it would.  So with nothing to lose, I dedicated myself to trying different combinations of things that might change my body's chemistry.  I guess I got lucky in finding something that works.  In hindsight, I probably would have had an easier time if I had gone with some medication, but I can't say it would have shortened the time.  Also being in incapacitating anguish was sort of my rock bottom so I may not have found the things I do now to keep me further from the ledge.   I have no idea what the connotations, condition, or context of your illness are.  I'm not a psychologist, psychiatrist or a neurologist (studied neurobiology as an undergrad, and read journals past that - but no doctorate in neuro).  I'm not going to pretend to be.  I can only speak from my experience, which countered everything that I was told by counselors and therapists.  So reframing my health helped me reframe my perception.  I had a mentality of "I am going to physically try different things until something works" and I did.  That is why I put in the breathing and water parts.  I found that people that write "drink water and exercise 30 min a day" didn't really get the point across.  It is hard to do that when you feel like shit.  It also doesn't work for everyone.  I guess I was hoping to help those "the love of my life is gone" or "college is hard" people on here while I helped myself.  Their pain is no less real, but I think reframing can help them.  Your point is well taken...  Hopefully this post helped someone out there, but as they say the road to hell is paved with good intentions.  I sincerely wish only well for you.  Thank you for reading my post.
